title: SQL Injection in Loan Eligibility Query

codeSnippet:
const query = `SELECT * FROM applicants WHERE income = ${req.body.income}`;
const result = await db.query(query);

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in Contact Notes
description: Contact notes entered by CRM users are rendered without output encoding, allowing a stored XSS payload to execute in the browser of any agent who later views the contact record.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in Feedback Form
description: The feedback screen reflects the 'subject' query parameter back into the page without escaping, allowing script injection via a crafted deep link.

title: Hardcoded JWT Signing Secret
description: The JWT signing secret used to issue session tokens is committed in plaintext in the auth service configuration file, allowing anyone with source access to forge valid tokens.

title: Hardcoded Database Credentials in Fraud Scoring Service
description: Database connection credentials for the fraud scoring datastore are hardcoded in the client module rather than sourced from the secrets manager.

title: Insecure Deserialization of Session State
description: Session state passed between the identity provider and downstream services is deserialized with Java's native ObjectInputStream without type validation, permitting remote code execution via a crafted payload.
codeSnippet:
ObjectInputStream in = new ObjectInputStream(request.getInputStream());
SessionState state = (SessionState) in.readObject();

title: Unsafe Dynamic Deserialization in Proxy Handler
description: The API gateway proxy handler deserializes upstream response bodies using an insecure YAML loader that permits arbitrary object instantiation.

title: OS Command Injection in Batch File Processor
description: The nightly batch file processor passes user-provided filenames directly to a shell command, allowing command injection via a crafted filename.

title: Command Injection in Backup Runner Script
description: The infrastructure backup runner shells out with an unsanitized hostname parameter, allowing command injection when triggered via the internal admin API.

title: SQL Injection in Document Search
description: The document management search controller builds a full-text search query by string concatenation, allowing SQL injection via the search term field.
codeSnippet: String sql = "SELECT * FROM documents WHERE title LIKE '%" + term + "%'";

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in Employee Directory
description: The employee directory profile page echoes the 'ref' query parameter into an inline script block without encoding.
falsePositiveReason: Query parameter is rendered inside a server-templated context that HTML-escapes the value before output; confirming with a manual PoC.

title: Hardcoded SMTP Credentials
description: SMTP relay credentials used by the notification service are embedded directly in the client configuration module.

title: Insecure Reflection-Based Report Loader
description: The treasury report generator instantiates report handler classes by name from user-controlled input using reflection, without an allowlist, enabling arbitrary class loading.

title: Command Injection in Vendor File Converter
description: The vendor document converter utility passes an unsanitized filename to a shell-invoked conversion tool, permitting command injection.

title: SQL Injection in Analytics Report Query Builder
description: The analytics warehouse's ad-hoc report builder interpolates user-selected column and filter names directly into raw SQL, allowing injection via crafted filter input.
codeSnippet:
query = f"SELECT {columns} FROM fact_transactions WHERE {filter_clause}"
cursor.execute(query)

title: Missing Security Headers on Notification Webhook Receiver
description: The inbound webhook receiver for the notification service does not set standard hardening headers on its responses.
requestSample:
POST /notify/webhook HTTP/1.1
Host: notify.internal
Content-Type: application/json

{"event":"test"}
responseSample:
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
(no X-Content-Type-Options or Strict-Transport-Security headers present)

title: Insecure API Endpoint Exposing Fraud Scoring Internals
description: The fraud scoring API returns internal model feature weights and thresholds in its response payload, which could allow an attacker to reverse-engineer detection logic.
requestSample:
POST /api/v1/fraud/score HTTP/1.1
Host: fraud-api.internal
Content-Type: application/json

{"transactionId":"TXN-88213"}

title: SQL Injection in ESB Route Configuration API
description: The enterprise service bus routing configuration API is vulnerable to SQL injection through the routeKey parameter used to look up routing rules.
requestSample:
POST /esb/api/route HTTP/1.1
Host: esb.internal
Content-Type: application/json

{"routeKey":"core' UNION SELECT username,password FROM admin_users--"}

title: Remote Code Execution via JNDI Lookup (Log4Shell)
description: log4j-core's JNDI message lookup substitution allows an attacker who can control log messages or parameters to execute arbitrary code loaded from an attacker-controlled LDAP server.

title: Command Injection via Template Function
description: lodash's template function allows a malicious template string to execute arbitrary shell commands via improper input sanitization.

title: Proxy-Authorization Header Leak
description: The requests library leaks the Proxy-Authorization header to destination servers when following cross-origin redirects through a proxy.

title: Deserialization RCE via Polymorphic Typing
description: jackson-databind's polymorphic type handling permits an attacker to supply a crafted payload that triggers remote code execution through gadget chains during deserialization.

title: Spring4Shell Remote Code Execution
description: A Spring MVC/WebFlux application running on JDK 9+ may be vulnerable to remote code execution via data binding, allowing an attacker to access the classloader and execute arbitrary code.

title: ReDoS in Trim Function
description: axios's trim utility uses a regular expression vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking, allowing a crafted string to cause a denial of service.

title: Prototype Pollution via Argument Parsing
description: minimist fails to properly sanitize `__proto__` in parsed arguments, allowing prototype pollution that can lead to denial of service or, in some code paths, remote code execution.

title: Arbitrary Code Execution via full_load
description: PyYAML's full_load and FullLoader methods are subject to arbitrary code execution when deserializing untrusted YAML input containing crafted Python object tags.

title: SQL Injection in GIS Functions
description: Django's GIS functions and aggregates on Oracle allow SQL injection via geometry values passed to internal query construction.

title: Deserialization Remote Code Execution
description: commons-collections' InvokerTransformer allows arbitrary method invocation during Java deserialization, enabling remote code execution via a crafted gadget chain.

title: Denial of Service via Deeply Nested JSON
description: Newtonsoft.Json can be forced into excessive recursion when deserializing deeply nested JSON, leading to a stack overflow and denial of service.

title: File Content Disclosure via Accept-Language Header
description: actionpack's render method can be tricked into disclosing arbitrary file contents from the server via a crafted Accept-Language header when rendering fails.

title: ReDoS via Crafted Authority Component
description: urllib3 has a catastrophic backtracking regular expression when parsing the authority component of a crafted URL, allowing a remote denial of service.
falsePositiveReason: Application pins a URL allow-list before requests reach urllib3; verifying whether the vulnerable code path is reachable.

title: Local Information Disclosure via Temp Files
description: JUnit4's TemporaryFolder rule creates temporary files and directories with world-readable permissions on Unix-like systems, exposing test data to other local users.

title: Open Redirect via Malformed URL
description: express's res.location and res.redirect can be manipulated with a malformed URL to redirect users to an attacker-controlled domain.

title: Denial of Service via Crafted Protobuf Message
description: protobuf-java's parsing of crafted messages with deeply nested groups can lead to excessive resource consumption and denial of service.
